name: Mortal Remains
english_description: A classic English-language LPMud, admin'd by "Cyanide" 1997-2000, running the public-domain-released source of the TMI-2 ("The Mud Institute") 1.4alpha mudlib base. The real mudlib root is the repo's `1.4alpha/` directory; a completely separate, unrelated bundled mudlib base (`lima-1.0a8/`, the Lima mudlib, its own self-contained lib/etc/driver-scaffolding) was excluded before conversion, matching this project's convention of ignoring bundled non-live codebases. A ~13,500-file, 66MB archive of real 1997-2000 wizard-home content across dozens of authors (Cyanide, Chronos, Nightmask, Spooner, and many more), full TMI-2 registration/character-creation (password, email, real name, then a menu-driven race/gender/handedness/alignment/stat-reroll wizard), and a real starting town (Decatur). Porting it surfaced several genuine driver-dialect bugs, the highest-impact being a fatal empty-array crash in master.lpc's author_file()/domain_file() (this driver's sane explode("/","/") returns a truly empty array, unlike the two-empty-strings the original code expected, aborting master's own boot before a single connection could be accepted), a recurring 'inherit after global variables' typo across dozens of independently-authored files (worst instance: std/monster.lpc, the universal NPC base class, whose fix alone recovered ~1770 cascading compile failures), a `ref` reserved-word collision in the preloaded channel daemon, a `private inherit`-plus-qualified-super-call combination this driver's compiler flatly rejects even from the declaring file itself (std/user/tsh.lpc), the classic valid_write()/valid_read() bare-equality-vs-extension-appended-filename bug (denied every player's own save, breaking registration at password confirmation), and -- the most severe, silently blocking every single new character from ever completing registration -- an ACL helper (adm/simul_efun/overrides.lpc's exec() wrapper) checking `deep_inherit_list()` output against a bare "std/body.lpc" string when this driver's deep_inherit_list() always returns a leading-slash-prefixed "/std/body.lpc", so exec()-based body possession was denied unconditionally. A completely orphaned, unreferenced legacy object-system snapshot (`adm/AFD/`, ~870 files) is bundled in the archive but inherited by nothing in the live game tree; left in place undocumented as dead code, not deleted. The preloaded channel daemon makes a genuine outbound socket-connect attempt to a real (now long-dead) 1999-era Intermud-3 router address at every boot -- intended upstream behavior, not a bug, but flagged per this project's convention against automated high-frequency reboot loops for libs with a real network side effect.
